stem: During assessment of a child with short stature, which associated problem most supports a secondary pathological cause due to nutritional insufficiency?
explanation: Feeding problems most strongly suggest nutritional insufficiency as a secondary pathological cause of short stature.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Assessment of Childhood Short Stature

optionExplanations.A: Correct because feeding problems can indicate inadequate nutritional intake, which is a secondary pathological cause of short stature.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a delayed pubertal growth spurt suggests constitutional delay of growth and puberty, not nutritional insufficiency.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because male sex is associated with constitutional delay in some children, but it does not specifically point to nutritional insufficiency.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a height close to mid-parental height supports familial short stature rather than secondary pathological growth failure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because no red flags makes a physiological cause more likely and does not support nutritional insufficiency.
